title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 5: Excellence and Ethics in Appellate Practice
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 5 'Excellence and Ethics in Appellate Practice': CJP on the standards of integrity, propriety, and excellence expected of appellate justices and advocates
sub_topics: Justices as recluses who must be pure and appear pure ('the gods of Padre Faura')
CJP's own practice of avoiding audiences and calls on pending matters
Excellence and ethics in appellate advocacy
The duty of both bench and bar to propriety
signature_phrases: justices are better read than heard

stances.claim: Appellate justices must not only be pure but appear pure, avoiding even private audiences on pending matters.

notable_anecdotes: He notes receiving about thirty speaking invitations a year but declining most to avoid impropriety.
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 5, 'Excellence and Ethics in Appellate Practice,' sets out the standards expected of appellate justices and advocates. CJP observes that justices — 'the gods of Padre Faura' — must be pure and appear pure, recounts his own practice of avoiding audiences, visitors, and calls about pending matters, and urges both bench and bar to combine excellence with unimpeachable ethics.
